patch.value: A runtime schema field may take the name of a built-in read option (full, fields, compact), after which that option stops working for the command

Observed while testing update-many admission in a scratch tracker. pm schema add-field full --type string --commands create,list is accepted, and so are fields, compact, brief and include_body; only status is refused. Afterwards a get with the full option no longer returned the complete item projection in the SDK spec that registered the field, and the bulk planner clears list.fields, list.full, list.compact and list.brief, so a filter on such a field cannot reach a bulk selection (update-many now refuses that key by name). The schema should refuse a field whose option spelling collides with a declared option of a command it is registered for, as it does for status.

schema add-field refuses an option-spelling collision per registered command with a typed refusal naming the option; pm validate reports existing fields that collide; A spec covers full, fields and compact for list and get
schema add-field refuses a name or alias that collides with a declared option of a command the field is registered for, naming the option
The field is accepted and silently shadows or is shadowed by the built-in option

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Implementation evidence (2026-11-22).

Reproduced on the released build in a scratch tracker: after schema add-field full --commands create,list, pm list --full returned count 0 with filters.runtime_filters reading the flag as a field filter, so the defect is a silent wrong answer and not only a lost projection. Cause: the CLI reuses an existing option of the same name instead of adding a second one, so one flag carries two meanings.

Rule. A field is refused when its key, flag or any alias equals a built-in option of a command it is registered for. The built-in side is read from the command's declared flag contract (the same source the parser registers from), so no second list exists. The key is compared as well as the flags because the parsed value is stored under the key whatever the flag is spelled, and a negated built-in such as no-pager reserves pager. Collisions are evaluated per registered command, so full is still accepted for create.

Declared exception. The shipped ops profile defines severity on create and update, where it deliberately replaces the built-in severity option. The exemption is derived from the reserved-key list (item metadata a custom field is allowed to redefine), and it covers the field's own key only. An alias severity on a differently named field is refused: probed with a stored field, the flag wrote both the built-in and the custom field and the built-in validator refused custom values.

Surfaces. schema add-field and profile apply (dry run included) refuse with schema_field_option_collision, exit 2, naming every shadowed option per command and the narrower commands list when one exists. profile lint reports field_option_collision as an error. validate --check-metadata reports stored fields as validate_schema_field_option_collision with rows, a truncation flag and a fix hint, and adds no keys when there are none.

Census before tightening. The three shipped profiles and this repository's tracker report zero collisions. Four existing specs registered names the rule refuses (allow_missing_parent, path, token_budget, compact, and the severity alias); they now store such fields directly, as a tracker created by an earlier release would hold them, so the behaviour for stored fields stays covered.

Not covered. Fields an extension registers through registerItemFields do not pass through this check. The acceptance criterion names get, but get is not a command a field can be registered for; the spec covers list, search and context.

patch.value: 13 spec cases pass, the new module is at 100 percent coverage, shipped profiles and this tracker report zero collisions, and pm list --full returns the seeded item after the refused registration
A field named like a built-in option is refused per registered command with the option named, stored collisions are reported by validate, and the built-in option keeps working

Added a shared SDK check that compares a field's key, flag and aliases with the declared flag contract of each registered command. schema add-field and profile apply refuse with schema_field_option_collision, profile lint reports field_option_collision, and validate reports already stored fields. The severity redefinition the ops profile relies on stays allowed.
Custom fields can no longer shadow a built-in option of a command they are registered for

value.negative_control: tests/unit/sdk/schema/field-option-collisions.spec.ts registers full, fields and compact for list, search and context and requires a named refusal and a working pm list --full; on the previous release the registration succeeds and pm list --full returns zero rows

value.text:
Review follow-up on PR 1768 (2026-11-22). Two findings from the hosted review were confirmed and fixed.

1. Punctuated aliases bypassed the check. The first version compared names after removing only hyphens and underscores, but the reader of field values treats any punctuation as a word break, so an alias token.budget also reads tokenBudget and shadowed the list token budget option. The comparison now takes its keys from that reader (resolveCandidateOptionKeys) plus the parser's own attribute for the flag, on both the field side and the built-in side.

2. schema rename-field wrote a target definition without the check. The migration runner now applies the shared refusal to the target definition before a plan is stored or previewed, so a dry run refuses as well, the fields file is unchanged and item values stay under the old key. A target that already exists is treated as a resumed migration and is not re-judged.

The profile lint finding moved from the core lint to the profile lint command so that the authoring entry point's lint does not depend on the command flag contracts.

Specs added for a dotted and a colon alias and for the rename refusal (dry run and real). The collision module and the schema migration module both measure 100 percent in a focused coverage run.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Second review round on PR 1768 (independent local review, 2026-11-22). Findings verified against the code and fixed in this item:

- Negated options. A negated built-in such as no-notes is parsed under notes and delivered to handlers as noNotes; only the first was reserved, so a field keyed no_notes with another flag still received the built-in option's value. Both keys are now reserved. The negation is removed once, as the parser does, so a doubled prefix is no longer refused by mistake.
- Severity exemption. It applied to any spelling that normalised to severity. It now requires the field key to be exactly a redefinable metadata key and the spelling to be that same name.
- Rename guard. A same-named field defined inline in settings for another command made a new rename look like a resumed one and skipped the check. The guard now skips only when a stored migration plan exists.
- Retry hint. The narrower commands list printed the command path (update-many) where the option accepts update_many.
- Repair hint. validate and the remediation entry recommended remove then add, which leaves item values under the old key; they now recommend rename-field, a same-key re-registration for a flag or command change, and a settings edit for an inline definition.
- Shared lint. The finding had been moved to the profile lint command, so a package's assertProjectProfile check passed a profile that apply refuses. It is back in the shared lint; the authoring entry point already loads the flag contracts, so there is no import cost.
- Spec. Each row now runs its own command with its own option before and after and requires an unchanged answer.
- Documentation. The scope expiry sentence now says the layer ends when the scope call itself has completed.

Left to follow-up items because they predate this change or are other write paths: flag spellings the parser splits or already owns implicitly (a pipe in a flag, the short help flag), and field definitions written inline through the extension settings mutation.
